title: Intrinsic anomalous Hall response in the bilayer kagome ferromagnet Co$_3$Sn
authors: Yuqi Qin, Soumya Sankar, Xingkai Cheng, Yifan Jiang, Shiming Lei, Junwei Liu, Berthold Jäck
abstract: Transition-metal kagome magnets provide a rich platform for investigating the interplay between layer stacking, magnetic order, and band topology. Here, we report the molecular beam epitaxy and experimental investigation of high-quality thin films of the kagome metal Co$_3$Sn, which has not been synthesized in bulk form yet. Structural and chemical analyses confirm a hexagonal lattice structure ($P6_3/mmc$) composed of direct A-B stacked Co$_3$Sn kagome bilayers. Magnetometry reveals robust easy-plane ferromagnetism with a Curie temperature exceeding $300\,\text{K}$. Magneto-transport measurements demonstrate metallic behavior (carrier density $n\approx5.01\times10^{22}\,\text{cm}^{-3}$) alongside a temperature-independent anomalous Hall conductivity of $σ_{\rm AHE}\approx90\,Ω^{-1}\cdot{\rm cm}^{-1}$, extending from $2\,\text{K}$ up to room temperature. Results from first-principles density functional theory calculations attribute this anomalous Hall response to intrinsic Berry curvature hotspots near the Fermi level in the spin-split band structure. Our results establish Co$_3$Sn as a room-temperature kagome ferromagnet and highlight the impact of the layer stacking sequence on the material properties of kagome metals from the CoSn family.
summary: This work reports the synthesis and characterization of $	ext{Co}_3	ext{Sn}$, a room-temperature kagome ferromagnet thin film. Experimentally, the material exhibits a large, temperature-independent anomalous Hall effect. Theoretically, the AHE is successfully linked to intrinsic Berry curvature hotspots calculated from the material's spin-split band structure.
main_problem: The study investigates the intrinsic anomalous Hall response in the bilayer kagome ferromagnet $	ext{Co}_3	ext{Sn}$.
main_result: The material exhibits robust easy-plane ferromagnetism and a large, temperature-independent anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{	ext{AHE}} \approx 90 \ \Omega^{-1} \cdot 	ext{cm}^{-1}$), which is theoretically attributed to intrinsic Berry curvature hotspots.
method: The research combines experimental techniques like Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE) and magneto-transport measurements with first-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is high-quality thin films of $	ext{Co}_3	ext{Sn}$, a kagome metal, grown epitaxially in a bilayer stacking sequence. The electronic properties are analyzed using DFT to map the spin-split band structure and Berry curvature.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{	ext{AHE}}$), magnetic anisotropy (easy-plane ferromagnetism), and the Berry curvature hotspots near the Fermi level.
important_parameters: Curie temperature ($T_C > 300\,	ext{K}$), carrier density ($n\approx5.01	imes10^{22}\,	ext{cm}^{-3}$), and the temperature independence of $\sigma_{	ext{AHE}}$ up to room temperature.
main_assumptions: The anomalous Hall response is assumed to be dominated by the intrinsic Berry curvature effect, which is confirmed by matching DFT calculations to experimental transport data.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the kagome structure, characterization results (XRD, XPS, $M(H)$ isotherms showing easy-plane ferromagnetism), and transport measurements showing the temperature-independent AHE.
paper_structure: The paper follows a standard structure: synthesis and structural characterization (MBE, XRD, XPS) $ightarrow$ magnetic characterization (Magnetometry) $ightarrow$ transport measurements (Hall effect, AHE) $ightarrow$ theoretical modeling (DFT calculation of Berry curvature) $ightarrow$ conclusion linking theory and experiment.
why_interesting: While not directly related to quantum information, the study of topological electronic properties (Berry curvature) in magnetic materials is foundational to understanding emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter physics, which underpins quantum computing hardware.
